measures.title: Constitutional Measure No. 1 (House Concurrent Resolution No. 3003, 2025 Session Laws, Ch. 614)
measures.summary: Placed on the ballot by the 2025 Legislative Assembly, this measure would amend section 9 of article III and section 16 of article IV of the North Dakota Constitution. It would require every proposed constitutional amendment, whether referred by the Legislature or proposed by citizen initiative, to receive at least 60% of the votes cast on the question to pass, instead of a simple majority. The estimated fiscal impact is none.
measures.yesMeans: You approve requiring future constitutional amendments to win at least 60% of the vote to be enacted.
measures.noMeans: You reject the change; constitutional amendments would continue to pass with a simple majority.

measures.title: Initiated Constitutional Measure No. 2
measures.summary: A citizen-initiated amendment adding a new section to article VIII of the North Dakota Constitution that would require all public school districts, public schools and public charter schools to provide one breakfast and one lunch each school day to enrolled students at no cost; nonpublic, Bureau of Indian Education and other tribal schools could choose to do the same. The state would reimburse schools at 100% of its current free-meal rates, adjusted yearly for inflation, with the Legislature required to find a funding source or else pay from the legacy earnings fund. The estimated fiscal impact is a $124.3 million to $134.3 million increase in ongoing spending for the 2027-2029 biennium, adjusted for inflation after that.
measures.yesMeans: You approve requiring free breakfast and lunch for students in public schools, paid for by the state.
measures.noMeans: You reject the measure, and the constitution is not changed.
